::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will explain why a one-line change to a notebook produces a noisy diff, and name four ways to make the change reviewable.
- **Before you start:** [Save Point](../crypt/shield-of-undo.html) (for `git diff`), and two tiny mock notebooks, [before.ipynb](../../exercises/scriptorium/before.ipynb) and [after.ipynb](../../exercises/scriptorium/after.ipynb) (about 2.5 KB each, mock files). Save both into an empty folder.
- **Time:** about 15 minutes.
:::

## A notebook is a JSON file

You need this before an agent edits a notebook for you: if you cannot see what changed, you cannot review it. A `.ipynb` file is a JSON document. A code cell stores its source, an `execution_count` (the run counter) and its outputs, and a plot is stored in the file as a base64 string (the image bytes written out as text). Source and outputs share one file, so any run rewrites lines next to the code.

This is what git sees, with or without an agent. The two mock notebooks differ by one real change: the cutoff `30` became `40`. Compare them:

```bash
diff before.ipynb after.ipynb
```

```
5c5
<    "execution_count": 3,
---
>    "execution_count": 7,
8c8
<     "print(len([r for r in reads if r >= 30]))"
---
>     "print(len([r for r in reads if r >= 40]))"
15c15
<       "3\n"
---
>       "2\n"
21c21
<       "image/png": "AAECAwQFBgcICQoLDA0ODxAREhMUFRYXGBkaGx...
---
>       "image/png": "AAMGCQwPEhUYGx4hJCcqLTAzNjk8P0JFSEtOUV...
```

Four spots changed, and one of them is the code. The rest is the run counter, the printed result and an image blob. A real notebook has more cells and bigger images, so the code change is harder to find.

The risk is the same with a coding agent as with a human: a reviewer who cannot find the code change may approve without reading it.

## Four ways to make changes reviewable

Each option moves the noise somewhere else.

- **nbstripout:** strips outputs when git stores the notebook, so outputs stay in your working file only. Cost: each collaborator runs `nbstripout --install` themselves, because git does not copy filter settings (a filter is a program git runs on a file as it stores it) when someone clones the repository.
- **jupytext:** pairs the `.ipynb` with a `.py` file. You review the `.py`, and outputs stay in the `.ipynb`.
- **nbdime:** a notebook-aware diff and merge tool. Everyone reviewing needs it installed.
- **marimo:** a notebook tool that stores notebooks as pure Python, so ordinary git diffs work.

## Review the code cells

Whatever you choose:

- Run `git diff --stat` before committing and look for a notebook that grew by megabytes.
- Read the source cells, and regenerate outputs instead of reviewing them. An output in a diff shows that something ran once; a re-run shows whether the code produces it.

## With an agent

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Claude Code reads a `.ipynb` with all its cells and outputs, so an output-heavy notebook fills the context window (the text the agent can hold at once). When an agent edits a code cell, that cell's saved outputs and execution count are cleared, so the diff shows lost outputs as well as new source.

`nbstripout` leaves outputs in the working file, so the agent still reads them. To keep the agent on the code, strip outputs from the working copy (nbstripout's pre-commit mode does this) or point the agent at the paired `.py`.

## OpenCode + Ollama

The idea is the same: review the source cells. Check OpenCode's docs for how it handles notebook files.

:::

::: {.ao-lore}
## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [The Notebook file format](https://nbformat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format_description.html): nbformat, docs. Why read: it is the spec showing that a notebook is JSON holding outputs, execution counts and base64 images, which explains the noisy diffs.
- [nbstripout](https://github.com/kynan/nbstripout): nbstripout project (GitHub), repo. Why read: it strips outputs from a notebook with a Git filter set up by `nbstripout --install`, so Git never sees them.
- [Jupytext](https://github.com/jupytext/jupytext): jupytext project (GitHub), repo. Why read: it pairs an .ipynb with a plain .py so reviewers diff the code only.
- [nbdime](https://nbdime.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): nbdime project, docs. Why read: it gives notebook-aware diff and merge tools if you must keep .ipynb in Git.
- [marimo documentation](https://docs.marimo.io/): marimo, docs. Why read: it describes a notebook stored as plain Python, so Git diffs show code only; this is the format option the quest compares.
:::
